content:
alex: Auditor wants a session provenance artifact for ephemeral KMS keys used during the 03/01 incident. They specifically asked for: chain-of-custody, IAM role assumption logs, and the exact KMS key versions and policies applied. asking for 90-day window.

maria: Ack. Do we already have an export workflow for session-level traces? I know we produce CloudTrail+KMS logs and STS AssumeRole events but we usually sample.

liam: We can pull a combined export: CloudTrail (management events) + KMS CloudWatch logs + STS logs from CloudTrail lookup. I can script an export that includes requestIDs for correlation.

rachel: For the auditor, they want a readable manifest. Please include: artifact list, time range, export commands used, and a brief statement of collection methodology. Also include checksums for each exported file. :white_check_mark:

alex: Good call. Auditor also asked about ephemeral session key rotation policy and whether session keys ever persist to S3. Short answer: sessions are ephemeral, we don't persist raw data, but some logs in S3 (CloudTrail) will contain request metadata.

liam: Draft export commands (will run in staging first):
```bash
# export CloudTrail events for STS and KMS in timeframe
aws cloudtrail lookup-events --lookup-attributes AttributeKey=EventName,AttributeValue=AssumeRole --start-time 2025-02-01T00:00:00Z --end-time 2025-03-31T23:59:59Z > assume-role-events.json
aws cloudtrail lookup-events --lookup-attributes AttributeKey=EventName,AttributeValue=Encrypt --start-time 2025-02-01T00:00:00Z --end-time 2025-03-31T23:59:59Z > kms-encrypt-events.json
# list KMS key versions/policies
aws kms get-key-rotation-status --key-id alias/redwood-inference-main > kms-rotation.json
aws kms get-key-policy --key-id alias/redwood-inference-main --policy-name default > kms-policy.json
```

maria: Can we redact IAM principal ARNs for internal engineers in the export before handing to auditor? We need to discuss PII/ops privacy. Auditor asked for names/roles though.

rachel: We should follow principle of least disclosure. Provide role names and service principals; redact personal account identifiers (e.g., internal user emails) unless auditor has NDA scope that includes them. Add a short justification in the manifest.

auditor_jane: Hey team — we do need role and service principal identities to map to control owners, but personal user emails can be redacted. Please include mapping file that shows role -> team owner. Signed attestation from security that redaction was applied is fine.

alex: Noted. Liam, can you add a mapping CSV: role,owner,owner-email? redact owner-email if necessary. Also add a link to the RBAC change PRs that affected the timeframe (we had a few role updates in Feb).

liam: Will do. For traceability I'm also going to include the commit SHAs for the IaC that applied the role changes and the audit log snippets showing the effective policy at the time.

rachel: For the ephemeral key provenance, include KMS GenerateDataKey calls and the corresponding Encrypt/Decrypt operations with request IDs so we can tie which service session used which key material. Those entries are in CloudTrail, but ensure we surface the KMS RequestId fields.

forensics-bot: automated note: when exporting CloudTrail, include --include-management-events true and filter for EventSource: "kms.amazonaws.com" and EventName: ["GenerateDataKey", "Encrypt", "Decrypt", "ReEncryptTo", "ReEncryptFrom"] to capture full key activity.

alex: Thanks. One more ask from auditor: provide timeline for incident response actions (who assumed which role when, which runbooks were executed). Can we compile a condensed incident timeline?

maria: I can assemble the timeline from PagerDuty notes + incident doc + runbook execution logs. Will attach references.

liam: Plan: run exports in staging, run checksums, generate manifest + role mapping CSV, produce redaction log, and submit to rachel for attestation. ETA 48 hours.

rachel: Sounds good. I'll review and add attestation language and then share via secure file transfer. Auditor, we'll notify you when the package is ready and include a verification checklist.

auditor_jane: Thanks — that's exactly what we need. Quick Q: will you include a sample of decrypted KMS usage? We don't need plaintext, just proof that decryption occurred under expected roles.

alex: We'll include decryption event entries with RequestId, principal, and outcome status (Success/Failure) but no plaintext.

maria: Logging action items: 1) Liam: exports + manifest + checksums + role mapping (48h). 2) Maria: timeline + runbook refs. 3) Rachel: attestation + secure delivery. 4) Alex: coordinate redaction policy confirmation.

liam: Copy. Starting export now. Posting progress in this thread. :computer:

forensics-bot: automated note: export job started (job-id: fx-2025-03-kms-001). Will ping when complete.
